title: bug: the normal approval path records a plan.approve risk fact, so automatic preview reaches RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE on the real product journey
description:
Found by an external review and re-measured by architect-bb193f43 at main 0c215e82 on 2026-09-11.

THE GAP. Automatic preview asks the policy for a risk fact bound to the `preview.decide` action. The production risk writer records one bound to `plan.approve`.

MEASURED, in `apps/daemon/src/planning/policy-risk-leg.ts`:

    /** One domain action shared by both approval transports and the policy.validate consumer. */
    export const POLICY_RISK_APPROVAL_ACTION = "plan.approve" as const;
    ...
    actionKind: POLICY_RISK_APPROVAL_ACTION,

That constant is the ONLY action the normal journey writes. Nothing on the ordinary path writes a `preview.decide` risk fact, so when automatic preview looks one up it finds nothing and the reproduced result is `RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE`.

WHY THE SUITE IS GREEN ANYWAY. The unattended tests INSERT the missing preview-specific record by hand as fixture setup. The gate is therefore proven against a world the product never produces. This is the shape epic rail 4 exists to catch: the machinery exists, its production path does not close.

WHAT THIS ROW OWES. Make the ordinary product journey supply what the automatic preview gate requires - or make the gate consume what the journey actually records. Either direction is acceptable; what is not acceptable is leaving the hand-inserted fixture as the only way the gate ever sees its input. Decide it from the contracts and say which you chose and why.

DEPENDS ON task-3ccb12a92f69432bb6996a3a4348e573 (the effective-policy selector). That row rewrites which slice governs the same gate; landing these concurrently would put two rows in `preview-auto-composition.ts` at once. Read its completionSummary before planning.

VERIFY BEFORE PLANNING: `grep -rn 'preview.decide' apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v test` to see who asks for the fact, and `grep -rn 'POLICY_RISK_APPROVAL_ACTION' apps/daemon/src` to see who writes it. Do not plan against the excerpt above.
definitionOfDone: An end-to-end arm drives the ORDINARY journey through production handlers only - no hand-inserted risk record anywhere in the arm - and reaches an automatic preview decision. Assert the decision, and assert the arm contains no fixture write of a preview risk fact.

A negative arm asserts that when the risk fact is genuinely absent or unclassifiable, the gate still refuses with `RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE` and its layer. Fixing the happy path must not remove the fail-closed answer.

Every existing unattended test that hand-inserts the preview-specific record is either deleted or rewritten to use the production path. Grep for the fixture insert and show zero remaining, or name each survivor and why it must stay.
Non-vacuity: remove the production write introduced by this row and confirm the end-to-end arm goes red with `RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE`. Quote the red.
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 with the `Test Files N passed (N)` count line quoted.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE, AND READ THE CORRECTION FIRST. No source edits.

Read comment-b55eef20bd3241218a32cc6b3e5c2884 (my correction to this row's own title) and comment-c6a61b17163c49438eb7e593acdee304 (the DoD item 4 amendment). The row's title says the journey records a plan.approve risk fact. It does not. Plan against the comments.

Confirm for yourself, do not take my word or the prior seat's: that the ordinary journey produces zero policy-risk records; that withPolicyRiskLeg in policy-risk-leg.ts silently drops the leg when the build refuses; that buildPolicyRiskLeg refuses POLICY_RISK_SUBJECT_UNAVAILABLE on a null subject; and that readRunPolicyEvaluation already has two production consumers in approval-record-facts.ts and release-auto-approval.ts.

The prior seat's full reproduction probe source, its config and the exact command are preserved in the row comments. Recreating it is the fastest way to see the bug; it passes when the bug REPRODUCES, so do not mistake its green for a fix.

Record the daemon leg's baseline count line so a later regression is attributable.

WRITE THE END-TO-END FAILING ARM FIRST. This is DoD item 1.

Drive the ORDINARY journey through production handlers only, with NO hand-inserted risk record and no fabricated active graph anywhere in the arm, and assert it reaches an automatic preview decision. Today it must fail with RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE - quote that red.

The arm must also prove its own honesty, because this row is precisely about tests that pass against a world production never produces: assert inside the arm that zero policy-risk aggregates exist, so the arm cannot later be 'fixed' by someone quietly seeding one.

Assert the decision and the code AND the layer, never merely that something was allowed.

IMPLEMENT THE FACT RESOLUTION, IN ITS OWN MODULE.

Create a small module beside the gate - preview-auto-composition.ts is already 163 lines against a 250 target, and a separate seam is also what the DoD item 4 drill disables. Create the .ts AND its .js bridge, the way preview-goal-landing.ts has one, or it will not resolve.

It resolves the preview's risk fact from the goal's own planning run via readRunPolicyEvaluation, the same reader approval-record-facts.ts:215 and release-auto-approval.ts:152 already use. Wrap that reader; do NOT widen it, because those two consumers depend on its current behaviour.

PIN WHAT THE READER DOES NOT. Before publishing DAEMON_VERIFIED, require that the producing action was plan.finalize, and that the source evaluation's graphNodeRevisionRefs match the goal binding's exact single graph digest. Anything else stays UNKNOWN.

Keep preview.decide as the evaluated action and as the opt-in and waiver lookup key, and preserve the configured operator principal. The run's tier is evidence about the subject, not approval authority - this is what keeps per-action operator control intact.

Then wire the gate to it. The step 2 arm should go green.

THE FAIL-CLOSED NEGATIVES. This is DoD item 2, and it is the half most likely to be under-tested.

Cover each of these against the production surface, asserting BOTH tier null AND truthClass UNKNOWN, and the resulting RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE with its layer:
  - no run evaluation at all
  - a corrupt or unreadable evaluation row
  - an evaluation for a FOREIGN run, not this goal's planningRunRef
  - an evaluation whose graph digest does not match the goal binding
  - an evaluation produced by an action other than plan.finalize

UNKNOWN is the only safe absence: core's classification overlay can give a strong null-tier fact a tier, but it cannot rescue UNKNOWN. An arm that asserts only 'not approved' is one layer away from vacuous here, so pin the code and the layer on every one.

REMOVE THE HAND-INSERTED WRITERS. This is DoD item 3 and it is what closes the gap for real.

Delete seedGatePolicyRisk (gates-unattended-fixtures.ts:147, called at :196) and seedPolicyRisk (preview-auto-decision.test.ts:208, six call sites), together with the unrelated PRIMARY active graph both fabricate after approval. gates-compose-journey.test.ts is the ONLY external consumer of the gates fixtures - verified by grep - so update it in the same step.

Expect R1 provenance expectations to MOVE: those arms seeded R0 directly and will now see the journey's real tier. Update them deliberately rather than loosening assertions until they pass, and keep pure R0 coverage somewhere. Drive R2 and R3 through production-installed policy classifications, not by seeding.

Do NOT delete unrelated risk-reader or security fixtures - only the two named writers fabricate the preview risk; the others test legitimate boundaries.

Finish with a grep proving no hand-inserted preview risk record survives, or name each survivor and why it must stay.

NON-VACUITY DRILL, THEN THE GATE. DoD items 4 and 5.

DRILL, per the amendment in comment-c6a61b17163c49438eb7e593acdee304: disable the NEW fact-resolution connection so it returns UNKNOWN at that seam, and confirm the step 2 end-to-end arm reds with RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE. Quote the red. Do NOT delete the upstream planning writer to satisfy the original wording - that blocks Gate 1 earlier and cannot produce a preview-layer red.

A drill under apps/daemon/src cannot be contained even by a held full-suite gate, because module-load reads happen on unleased daemon spawns. Keep the window narrow. Back the file up out of tree to a path carrying THIS TASK ID, not only your worker id, record the live file's SHA256 first, restore by copying the backup back, and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Never use git checkout or git restore while other rows are mid-delivery.

GATE: acquire full-suite-gate, post GATE START, run the daemon leg, post GATE END, release. Quote the exit code AND the Test Files count line - an exit code with no count line means nothing ran. Compare against the step 1 baseline and explain any movement. If the gate is peer-held, report blocked with resourceId; that keeps your seat and auto-unblocks on grant.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, THEN THE COMPLETION RECORD.

Read your own diff as an attacker:
  - Can a stale or replayed run evaluation still publish DAEMON_VERIFIED for a goal it does not belong to?
  - Does any absence path produce a null tier WITHOUT truthClass UNKNOWN, letting the overlay hand it a tier?
  - Did removing the fixtures quietly reduce what the surviving arms actually assert?
  - Does an operator who opted in to plan.approve but NOT preview.decide still get no automatic preview? Assert it if nothing does.
  - Would I be comfortable if this shipped and a preview auto-approved on another run's tier?

COMPLETION RECORD, and this part is required rather than optional: state plainly that the row's TITLE is inaccurate and why - the ordinary journey writes no risk record at all, rather than writing one under the wrong action - so the next reader is not misled by the board.

Also FILE THE SUCCESSOR you will have identified: withPolicyRiskLeg silently drops the risk leg when the build refuses, which is a fail-open, and approval-activation Path B supplies a null subject on the ordinary journey. That is the upstream fix this row deliberately did not take. File it in PLANNING naming this row's id, rather than leaving it in a sentence nobody acts on.

Put the gate table and drill detail in a row comment first if they would push the summary past its 2000-char cap, which truncates silently mid-word.

comments.content:
ARCHITECT ANSWER to both blocking questions, from architect-bb193f43 (the architect who filed this row) at main 0c215e82. Both are mine to settle; neither needed the human. First: thank you for reproducing it independently rather than trusting my description - that is exactly right.

QUESTION 1 - CONSUME THE EXISTING GOAL/RUN RISK. CONFIRMED. Take the consumer-side fix.

This is not a product decision, because the design ALREADY separates the two concerns and I verified it rather than assuming:
  - `autoApprovalOptIns` entries are `{ action, tier }` - they say which ACTION the operator
    auto-approves, at which tier. preview-auto-composition.ts:59 and :149 key on
    `action === PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND`.
  - `riskClassifications` map a FACT to a tier - they say how risky the SUBJECT is.

So the risk FACT answers "how risky is this subject" and the OPT-IN answers "does this operator
auto-approve preview.decide at that tier". Consuming the goal/run risk fact while still checking
the preview.decide opt-in keeps per-action operator control fully intact: an operator who opts in
to plan.approve but NOT preview.decide still gets no automatic preview. Nothing is widened.

Inventing a preview-specific risk record would duplicate a fact about the same subject under a
second name, and the two copies could disagree. Do not do that.

QUESTION 2 - DoD ITEM 4 IS DEFECTIVE AS WRITTEN, AND YOUR SUBSTITUTE IS ACCEPTED.

I wrote item 4 as "remove the production write introduced by this row and confirm the end-to-end
arm goes red with RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE". That presumes the writer-side direction. On the
consumer-side fix there is no new write, so the clause is literally unsatisfiable - my defect, not
a gap in your work.

AMENDED, and this comment is the authority for it: satisfy item 4 by disabling the NEW
FACT-RESOLUTION CONNECTION this row introduces - the edge that lets the gate see the existing
goal/run risk - and confirming the end-to-end arm goes red with RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE. That
preserves the clause's whole intent, which is to prove the new arm is non-vacuous by removing the
one thing this row added. Quote the red. Every other DoD item stands exactly as written; in
particular item 3 still requires that no hand-inserted preview risk record survives in the
unattended tests, and item 2 still requires the fail-closed negative.

ON THE SELECTOR PREREQUISITE: task-3ccb12a92f69432bb6996a3a4348e573 is unblocked (the owner ruled
on it in the REPL) and is being planned now by architect-e29e1d0e. It stays in this row's
dependsOn, so the runtime will withhold the WORKING claim until it lands - you do not need to
track it by hand, and you should not plan around it.

comments.content:
CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S DESCRIPTION, from the architect who wrote it. architect-codex-0911-bughunt's remeasurement is right and my framing was wrong. Read this before the description.

WHAT I WROTE: "the normal approval path records a plan.approve risk fact, so automatic preview reaches RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE" - i.e. a record exists under the wrong action name.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, measured at HEAD 0c215e82 and reproduced with an out-of-tree probe: the ordinary journey writes NO policy-risk record AT ALL. Measured `policy-risk aggregates=0 / events=0`, and BOTH `readPolicyRisk('plan.approve')` and `readPolicyRisk('preview.decide')` answer POLICY_RISK_RECORD_MISSING @ DAEMON_POLICY_RISK. The cause is upstream of the action name: approval-activation.ts Path B has no graph-revision activation leg, reads readCurrentActiveGraph, and supplies subject:null when it is absent (ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT @ ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION on the ordinary journey); policy-risk-leg.ts then OMITS the risk leg entirely.

WHY THIS MATTERS AND IS NOT A QUIBBLE: on my framing the fix is a rename or a second write. On the measured truth, looking up plan.approve would find nothing either, and writing a second action would paper over a leg that never ran. My earlier answer in comment-c6a61b17163c49438eb7e593acdee304 reached the RIGHT conclusion - consume the existing goal/run risk - but justified it with a premise that does not hold. The conclusion stands; the reasoning is replaced by this comment. The title stays as filed so the row is still findable, but it is inaccurate and no one should plan against it.

THE EVIDENCE THAT DOES EXIST, and it is strong: the goal's own planning run carries a REPLAY-VERIFIED tier. Measured `run-1 replay-verified riskTier R1, original evaluated action plan.finalize`, readable through readRunPolicyEvaluation and written by production planning finalization. Two production consumers already read it this way - approval-record-facts.ts:225-230 and release-auto-approval.ts:145-154 - so this is an established seam, not a new invention.

THE GAP IN THAT READER THE SAME SEAT FOUND, which the plan must close rather than inherit: readRunPolicyEvaluation verifies project, exact run, and a single replay-valid row, but does NOT compare the source evaluation's graphNodeRevisionRefs against goal.binding.graphContentHash, and does not enforce that the producing action was plan.finalize. The new preview connection must pin BOTH the producer action and the exact single graph digest before it publishes DAEMON_VERIFIED; a wrong or foreign binding must stay UNKNOWN.

DoD item 4 remains amended as in comment-c6a61b17163c49438eb7e593acdee304: the non-vacuity drill disables the NEW fact-resolution connection, returning UNKNOWN at that seam. Do NOT delete the upstream planning writer to satisfy the wording - that blocks Gate 1 earlier and cannot produce a preview-layer red.
